Thirty-five comments

Johnny Cope

Source: Planxty “Cold Blow And The Rainy Night”
I’ll quote from the sleevenotes.

“Johnny Cope” combines the well known song and hornpipe of the same name.How it arrived in Kerry-where it was learned from the great fiddler Padric O’Keefe will never be known but in its travels from Scotland it picked up four more parts and was collected by Seamus Ennis as a six part hornpipe."

↳ Posted by dafydd on September 13th, 2005.

Great tune. I know it from the Noel Hill and Tony Linnane album, on which Noel Hill uses a solo break to play this tune. You say you transcribed this from “Cold Blow and the Rainy Night;” did Noel Hill play on this album? I know he played on one or two of them. I was wondering if he also played it with Planxty.

↳ Posted by smw on September 13th, 2005.

No, he’s not on the album.It was released in 1974 and the band was Liam O‘Flynn,Andy Irvine,Christy Moore and Johnny Moynihan.They sing the song first and then Liam O’Flynn plays it solo.

Re: Johnny Cope

Further to Chad’s posting . . .

Would this be the same Margaret Barry (Mairead de Barra) of Abbeyfeale, Co. Limerick, the younger sister of Donal de Barra who was one of the leading figures in Comhaltas Ceoltoiri Eireann? She played whistle and flute (prize winner in the Listowel Fleadh in about 1978 or -79 with a wonderful rendition of ‘Colonel Frazer’) and moved to Dublin to study.

↳ Posted by Nico on March 4th, 2021.

Johnny Cope, X:5

This is my transcription of the late Liam O’Flynn’s performance on Planxty’s “Cold Blow and the Rainy Night” album from 1974. I couldn’t find a melodically accurate transcription of his version anywhere online, so did my own. I haven’t tried to notate piping ornaments in general, so the E music transcription is slightly simplified from what he actually plays, but I have appended an extra E* section at the end for information/alternatives.

On the album Liam O’Flynn plays the tune on a “flat set” of pipes in C, so to play this notation along to the recording (e.g. https://youtu.be/4jjsK0-TfOk), use a C whistle!

I have a downloadable Word.doc of my notation and several other settings and background info/links which may be acquired here: https://app.box.com/s/wws1uc9tjqeteiyohrdl3et48adu4aig

There’s an interesting, thorough background survey to the Irish sources and settings of this tune here: https://rushymountain.com/2017/10/06/johnny-cope, which supplements the Tunearch ones nicely. (https://tunearch.org/wiki/Annotation:Johnny_Cope_(1) & https://tunearch.org/wiki/Annotation:Johnny_Cope_(2))

T:Johnny Cope
C:Traditional
O:Kerry, Ireland; after Scottish originals
S:Liam O‘Flynn, after Padraig O’Keeffe
D:Planxty: Cold Blow and the Rainy Night (Polydor, 1974)
N:On the album Liam O’Flynn plays the tune on a “flat set” of pipes in C, so to play this notation to the recording, use a C whistle
Z:Jem Hammond 4:3:2021
R:Hornpipe
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:Ador

Re: Johnny Cope

Most transcriptions of this tune give the second and third parts as distinct, repeatable sections - as in X:1. Is this how the piece is commonly played? (How do YOU do it?). It’s always seemed to me that these melody lines are so similar that the second time through is merely a slight variation of the first. This is how it’s shown in the transcription of Ms Barry’s setting linked to Chad’s comment above: (http://www.rogermillington.com/tunetoc/johnnycopebarry.html). Does anybody else think that this this is the way to play it ?

Re: Johnny Cope (For String Instrument)

Here’s an excellent Seamus Ennis recording of the tune . He’s the pipes tuned sharp but not bang on. I just tuned a bit shy of G# to learn it. Mandolin/Bouzouki Tuning “close to” (F#-C#-G#-C#) pretty much the same as Liam O’Flynn’s version in C structure wise . I was surprised to find ear tuning to Ennis’s pipes brought out a wonderful tone from my Instrument.
